To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we used monoclonal antibodies to define the antigenic structure of horseradishes peroxidase and that we showed the existence of at least three distinct antigenic sites on the molecule.
nine monoclonal antibodies to horseradsh peroxidase recognize three distinct antigenic regions on this enzyme.
the active site of HRP is located in an epitope region that is distinct from the heme-binding site.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and use of a panel of monoclonal and polyclonal antibodies to HRP.
the development of an epitope map for HRP, and the results of our experiments indicate that there are at least three distinct regions on the molecule.
the development of a panel of MAbs that recognize distinct epitopes on HRP, and the use of these MAbs to map the location of these epitopes on the enzyme.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
epitopes I and III are located in separate antigen regions, that group II epitopes overlap with those in either group I or III, and that epitope 2A2 is located at the active site of HRP.
the epitopes recognized by these MAbs are located in three distinct regions on the enzyme.

the epitopes of HRP recognized by MAbs are: (1) heme-associated, (2) conformationally dependent, (3) located at or near the enzyme active site, and (4) located at a site that is not involved in heme binding.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the MAbs in group I recognized epitopes located on the surface of HRP, the MAbs in groups II and II recognized heme-associated determinants at or near the catalytic site of the enzyme, and MAb 2A2 recognized a conformational epitope involving both the heme and protein components of the active site.

the epitope map of HRP can be divided into three distinct regions: a group I epitope that is removed from the active center of the enzyme, two group II epitopes that overlap with group I, and a group III epitope that is located at or near the heme-binding site of the enzyme and that may include both a heme moiety-dependent and a conformation-dependent epitope.
the heme moietyl and the protein moiety of HRP have separate but overlapping regions of antigenic determinants.
The main takeaway from our work is that

epitope mapping with use of MAbs is a valuable tool for the analysis of antigenic sites on proteins and that the results of epitope mapping can be correlated with the biological activity of the protein.
the epitopes of the MAbs to HRP can be divided into at least three groups, two of which recognize heme-associated epitope(s) near the active site of HRP.
epitope mapping can be a powerful tool for understanding the structure and function of proteins.
